explanation: The I84V mutation reduces nelfinavir binding through a loss of favorable van der Waals contacts within the S1/S1' subpocket. Isoleucine's larger branched side chain (with its γ-methyl group) makes optimal hydrophobic packing interactions with nelfinavir at the 2.4 Å contact distance, whereas valine's smaller, more linear side chain creates a subtle cavity or looser fit that diminishes these stabilizing van der Waals interactions. This modest destabilization (~0.25 kcal/mol) reflects the delicate geometric requirements for inhibitor binding in this critical substrate-binding pocket, where even small reductions in side-chain volume propagate into measurable loss of binding affinity.
